## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches and my changes comply. Only `benchmark/` is touched, which has no Hard Rules section; no new files.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*`.

## Affected area

Benchmarks or performance

## Summary

- `python -m benchmark.heuristics_regret <run> --baseline <earlier run>` adds a run-to-run section. It compares each case's `cudnn_auto` time with the same case in the earlier run, matched on the configuration columns both runs record. Cases slower than `--regress` (default 1.2x) are split into two tables: the default plan changed (a dispatch change), or the plan stayed the same (a kernel, backend or measurement change). Cases whose default stopped running are listed separately. With `--fail`, a slower new default plan or a lost default exits 1.
- A results file with two rows of one leg for one case (the linear-attention CSVs) is skipped with a warning instead of aborting the report. A whole nightly run directory can now be passed.
- Inference result rows gain `attn_mask` (`top_left` / `bottom_right` / `no_mask`, the training suite's vocabulary) and `has_sink`. The alignment comes from one helper, `config_types.attn_mask`, which `benchmark_single_attention` also uses to build the graph, so the column cannot drift from the graph.

## Why

- **The regression report.** The nightly records the default-dispatch time on every case (#1848), but nothing compares it across runs, so a default plan that changes and slows down between two nightlies is only found by reading the raw results. The report lists such cases first, under "new default plan", apart from same-plan drift. The dispatch fix for the change that prompted this is a separate PR.
- **The columns.** The inference CSV did not say how a causal case was aligned or whether it carried a sink, so offline replays of the default dispatch had to reconstruct both from the config files. The suite builds `s_q == s_kv` context graphs top-left and chunks bottom-right. Placement keyed those as different classes, which is how a generated placement entry missed square prefills (fixed separately). That is invisible in the data today.

## Related issues

Follows #1848.

## API and compatibility impact

None outside `benchmark/`. CSV rows gain two trailing columns. `--baseline` pairs a case with rows whose column set contains, or is contained in, its own (so a run that added a column still pairs with its predecessor) and drops a case with more than one counterpart; training and inference CSVs never pair with each other.

## Testing

- `pytest benchmark/attention_inference/tests/`: 16 passed. New tests cover the baseline split (new plan / same plan / lost default, with a column the baseline predates), mixed training + inference directories where only one schema gained a column, skipping a duplicate-leg file, and the `attn_mask` vocabulary. Each fails on develop or on this PR's first head.
- `benchmark_single_attention.py --backend cudnn --phase context --causal` run as a script on an H100: builds and times as before.
- `python -m benchmark.heuristics_regret <run> --baseline <earlier run>` on two nightly result directories (the run pair described above).

+
+def attn_mask(phase: str, context_causal: bool, q_tokens: int, kv_len: int, sliding_window_size: Optional[int]) -> str:
+    """Diagonal alignment of the case's causal mask. A context square is top-left; a context chunk and every decode row sit at
+    the end of the sequence (bottom-right); a single decode row is unmasked unless a window anchors it."""
+    if phase == "context":
+        if not context_causal:
+            return "no_mask"
+        return "top_left" if q_tokens == kv_len else "bottom_right"
+    return "bottom_right" if q_tokens > 1 or sliding_window_size else "no_mask"

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `456c567d3fdf` against base `5aca5bea1319`.

The report and result columns are useful. Two nonblocking P2 items remain: mixed CSV schemas can hide a regression from --fail, and the PR description includes information that should stay in private records. The focused tests pass; the independent mixed-schema probe demonstrates the reporting gap.

**[P2] Match baseline columns within each compatible case schema** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/456c567d3fdfcf5d5b81ec60abf766508e10ae9c/benchmark/heuristics_regret.py#L117))

The global column union makes an unrelated CSV affect inference matching. An older inference file has no attn_mask, while an older training file already has it. Comparing whole run directories therefore retains attn_mask in cols; the new inference key includes it and the old inference key does not, so the inference case is silently dropped. In a synthetic control, a changed-plan regression returns 1 with --fail when comparing the inference files alone, but returns 0 after adding identical unrelated training CSVs to both directories. Match on columns shared by the corresponding benchmark schemas/candidate cases, and reject ambiguous matches rather than using a run-wide union. Add the mixed training-plus-inference case to the regression tests.

Evidence: probe-mixed-schema.py/log: inference-only matched1/new-plan-regression1/exit1; whole-run matchedonlyunchangedtraining/new-plan-regression0/exit0. Source training BenchmarkResult already records attn_mask, while this PR adds it to inference BenchmarkResult. Attribution: Introduced by the new baseline matching path; exposed by the schema transition in this same PR.

**[P2] Keep restricted study details in private records** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/456c567d3fdfcf5d5b81ec60abf766508e10ae9c/PR%20description))

The description includes SM107 timings and performance ratios, plus an internal workspace/session footer. Please move those details to the private study record and keep the public description to the regression class, validation scope and correctness results.

Evidence: precheck:E05a confirms the internal-path footer; the description's Why/Testing sections also contain restricted device-performance measurements. Exact values and internal locations are intentionally omitted here. Attribution: Current PR description; no credential disclosure or approval-blocking defect established.

Validation: Exact-head inference benchmark suite: 15 passed, with ten passing subtests. Independent actual-CLI synthetic CSV probe confirms that adding unrelated training data suppresses a changed-plan inference regression and changes --fail from exit1 to exit0. No GPU measurements were used. Traced the mask helper into graph construction and CSV result fields. Context-square, context-chunk and generation alignment behavior is unchanged. Reviewed duplicate-leg skipping, failed-default handling and CLI status paths. Style and Security passed. Existing pipeline 78178408 runs python/sdpa/misc; that target does not collect benchmark/attention_inference/tests, so the local unit run supplies the relevant test coverage. No duplicate GPU request.

Limitations: No nightly data or device timing study was rerun. The reproducer uses synthetic CSVs only. GPU CI remains pending and does not validate the new report's unit tests.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
